## 1.2.0

### Minor Changes

- #2401 `5aba6f4` Thanks @jie-dai_sfemu! - Regenerate the Shopper Orders SCAPI client from OAS v1.17.1 (was v1.10.0) to expose the OMS return/cancel surface. Adds the `returnOmsOrder`, `cancelOmsOrder`, and `getOmsMetaData` operations to `clients.shopperOrders.*`, the `quantityAvailableToReturn` / `quantityReturned` / `quantityReturnInitiated` fields on order product-item OMS data, and the `OmsMetaData`, `OmsReasonCode`, `OmsReturnOrderRequest`, and `OmsReturnProductItem` types. This is the shared SDK prerequisite (WI-0) for the item-level order return feature.

- #2436 `09aaafb` Thanks @jie-dai_sfemu! - Generate the Shopper Delivery Estimates SCAPI client (`shopperDeliveryEstimates`). Vendors the `shopper-delivery-estimates` OAS (v1.1.0, `getDeliveryEstimates`) and adds the generated types, operation map, and a built-in client exposed on `Clients`, following the existing built-in client pattern. Also registers the new client in the dev CLI catalogs (`sfnext scapi add` / `sfnext scapi available`) and the template's built-in override list.

- #2445 `fdc2127` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Add `getSitesFromDataStoreLazy` to read the global `ecomSitesData` entry from the MRT data store as a typed `DalSite[]`, exposing multi-site config (including `name` and `alias`) to loaders. The read is lazy — only routes that call the accessor pay for the data-store round trip, and results inherit the data-store L1 cache. Returns `null` when the entry is missing, malformed, or the producer synced zero sites, so callers can fall back to their static config. Opt into fail-fast with `SFNEXT_DATA_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_MODE=throw`.

- #2458 `a5ed773` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Add passkey registration upsell flow. After a shopper registers or logs in, an 8-second toast prompts them to create a passkey if their browser supports WebAuthn and they don't have one yet. Clicking the toast action opens a modal that walks them through passkey creation via the SCAPI WebAuthn registration flow.

  Adds the `clients.auth.passkey` namespace (`authorizeRegistration`, `startRegistration`, `finishRegistration`) to `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` to back this flow.

- #2458 `7419e3e` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Let shoppers name a passkey during creation, and show richer passkey metadata (created date, last-used date, use count, "New" badge) on the account passkeys page.

  Corrects the vendored `PasskeyCredential` schema in `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` — SCAPI's `getPasskeyUserByLoginId` already returns `aaguid`, `createdTime`, `lastUsed`, and `uses` per credential, but the vendored OpenAPI spec was missing these fields.

  Also hardens the passkey management flow: the account passkeys page 404s when the passkey feature is disabled, the add-passkey entry point surfaces an error on browsers that can't complete WebAuthn registration instead of opening a modal that can only fail, passkey nicknames are validated against SCAPI's 128-character limit on both the client and the start-registration action, deleting an already-absent credential is treated as success, and the delete action no longer triggers a redundant account-loader revalidation.

  Improves passkey UI reliability under slow or failing passkey-status conditions: the "set up a passkey" upsell toast now reads passkey status with a direct fetch and fires from that response, so it no longer gets stuck behind an in-flight page transition; and the account passkeys page renders its heading and "Add Passkey" button immediately, deferring only the credential list — if that list fails to load, an inline message appears in its place rather than blanking the whole page.

- #2032 `25272e5` Thanks @vcua_sfemu! - Add a single `app.cookies.domain` knob for the storefront cookie domain

  A new global config field, `app.cookies.domain`, sets the default `Domain` on **every** cookie the storefront writes — the auth/session cookies and the site-context cookies (`site_id`, locale, currency). Set it once via `PUBLIC__app__cookies__domain=.example.com` instead of redeclaring the entire `commerce.sites` array just to share cookies across subdomains.

  Precedence (applies to all storefront cookies): per-site `commerce.sites[].cookies.domain` → global `app.cookies.domain` → host-only scoping (the default; setting a domain is opt-in). The SDK site-context middleware now applies the resolved per-site domain when serializing the site-context cookies, so the per-site override reaches them too.

  Also fixes the stale `PUBLIC__app__site__cookies__domain` references in the docs (the path never existed).

- #1932 `35d961b` Thanks @mjuraschik_sfemu! - w:

  Embedded Content Blocks (ECB)

  Adds support for fetching and rendering Page Designer components outside
  of a page context. The header is wired up as the first embedded component,
  hosting an `announcement` region for the new announcement banner. Data
  collection for embedded components reuses the same `componentData` promise
  map that pages use, so streaming and per-component Suspense boundaries
  work the same way for both.

- #2366 `6ea4b59` Thanks @deepali-bharmal_sfemu! - `resolvePage` and `processPage` now handle embedded components in addition to pages. `IdentifierType` gains a `'component'` value; passing it routes directly through `getComponentManifest` (no assignment lookup, no variation selection) and skips the qualifier-context round-trip when the manifest's `requiresContext` flag is `false`. The visitor in `processPage` is shared between page and component flows; the entry point is selected by an explicit `kind: 'page' | 'component'` field on `PageProcessorContext` (defaults to `'page'` when absent). Public API names (`resolvePage`, `processPage`) are unchanged.

- #2132 `7af1edb` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix the dev hybrid proxy to handle every `url.prefix` shape out of the box, so a locale-prefixed legacy path (e.g. `/uk/cart`) is no longer double-stacked into `/s/{siteId}/{locale}/uk/cart`.

  The dev proxy unconditionally prepended `/s/{defaultSiteId}/{locale}` to every non-SFRA path. Now that the template emits prefixed paths (`/uk/cart`, `/global/en-GB/cart`), that stacked the locale a second time and SFRA 404'd. The proxy now reads `app.url.prefix` and the site/locale alias catalog from `config.server.ts`, strips the prefix the URL already carries, and reuses that site/locale when decorating to SFRA's `/s/{siteId}/{locale}/…` shape — for no prefix, `/:localeId`, and `/:siteId/:localeId` alike. A captured segment is only treated as a site/locale when it is a known identifier, so a bare legacy path (`/cart` under `/:localeId`) isn't mistaken for a locale home. The root `/` maps to the locale-less SFRA site root and the query string is preserved across the rewrite.

  `hybridProxyPlugin` gains optional `urlPrefix`, `siteAliases`, `localeAliases`, and a last-resort `rewritePath` escape hatch for non-standard URL models. `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` exports a new `extractPrefixParamValues` site-context helper (mirrors `stripPathPrefix`'s matching rules) that powers the prefix-aware rewrite.

- #2210 `8e720bf` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Add lazy data-store preference middleware and an opt-in cross-request L1 cache to cut DynamoDB reads on the single shared data-store partition

  The eager `dataStoreMiddleware` reads all four preference entries on every request that reaches root, even routes that never use them. All entries share one partition key (`"${MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID} ${DEPLOY_TARGET}"`), so that volume can throttle one physical partition under load.

  The new lazy variants (`customSitePreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `customGlobalPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `gcpPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `loginPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, their `get*Lazy` accessors, and the `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy` bundle) register a memoized loader instead of fetching up front, so the read fires only when a loader reads the value and repeat reads within a request share the promise. The eager exports are deprecated but unchanged. The template wires `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy`, reads login preferences via the async `getLoginPreferences` wrapper, and moves the GCP Address Autocomplete API key onto the checkout loader (the only route mounting `GoogleCloudApiProvider`).

  The L1 cache serves repeat reads of the same entry from memory. It lives on `globalThis` (via a `Symbol.for` key) to survive SSR module re-evaluation and persist across a warm Lambda's sequential requests. Only successful reads of deployment-/site-scoped preference entries are cached — never shopper data, fallbacks, missing entries, or errors; `getDataStoreEntry` stays a thin, cache-free read. It is off by default; set `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_ENABLED=true` to opt in per environment (e.g. deployed MRT). `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_TTL` sets the TTL in ms (default 300000) and `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_MAXBYTES` the total-value byte budget (default 131072); zero/negative/non-numeric falls back to the default. The cache is bounded by byte size, not entry count, evicting least-recently-used keys. `clearDataStoreCache()` drops the instance for test isolation or to force-bust a warm container after a preference publish.

- #2495 `463b2d1` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Add optional `offset`, `limit`, and `total` fields to the `ViewSearchEvent` and `ViewCategoryEvent` analytics events. These let the storefront report a product's position and page number across the full result set rather than restarting per page. The fields are optional, so existing event producers are unaffected.

- #2454 `959a001` Thanks @harshini-magesh_sfemu! - Forward a caller-supplied `query` (e.g. `{ expand: ['approaching_discounts'] }`) through the `getOrCreateBasket` basket helper onto the underlying `getBasket` calls, including the quota-error fallback. The SDK threads whatever expansions the caller requests without hardcoding a value, so templates can opt into basket expansions on the shared fetch.

- #2366 `6ea4b59` Thanks @deepali-bharmal_sfemu! - Add `ComponentManifest` type and `ManifestStorage.getComponentManifest` for the embedded-component (ECB) read path. Introduces a base `Manifest` interface (with `manifestType`, `context`, `componentInfo`) extended by both `PageManifest` and the new `ComponentManifest`, mirroring the backend hierarchy in `commerce/digital`. The Data Store-backed storage in `pageDesignerResolutionMiddleware` now resolves keys of the form `component-manifest_{site}_{id}` alongside existing page and site manifests, with the same fail-open semantics. No runtime behavior changes for pages.

- #2042 `c0b87fb` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Shopper agent (Embedded Messaging) now contributes its exact configured origins to the CSP instead of relying on broad wildcards. The security middleware accepts boot-static CSP contributors; the template ships a shopper-agent contributor that derives script/frame/connect origins from `commerceAgent` config. The SDK now exports `normalizeCspOrigin` / `inspectCspOrigin` — the single source of truth for CSP-origin safety rules, shared by the boot-time contributor validator and the template normalizer so they cannot drift. Adds the `add-csp-contributor` skill for authoring new contributors. No change to shipped headers when shopper agent is disabled.

- #2471 `c1ed55f` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Add a `commerce.sitesFromDal` flag (default on) that sources `commerce.sites` from the unified DAL sites entry. When on and the DAL entry is present, a new request middleware rewrites the site config for site/locale/currency resolution; otherwise the static config stands.

  Because the flag ships enabled, site/locale/currency resolution reads from the DAL sites entry once the matching Business Manager sync is enabled — making the DAL the source of truth for site configuration in that setup. If the DAL entry is missing, unavailable, or yields no usable sites, resolution falls back to the static `commerce.sites` in `config.server.ts`. To keep the static config authoritative regardless of the DAL, set `commerce.sitesFromDal` to `false` (or `PUBLIC__app__commerce__sitesFromDal=false`).

  `readLazyDataStoreEntry` now logs a warning when it finds no registered loader in context, so a lazy data-store middleware that is missing from (or misordered in) the request chain surfaces as a debuggable misconfiguration instead of a silent no-op.

- #2023 `37d9aee` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Stop marking cookies `Secure` in local development so Safari can persist them. The template's `getCookieConfig` (auth, basket, shopper-context, turnstile cookies) hardcoded `secure: true`, and the SDK's site-context cookies (`site_id`, `lng`, `currency`) gated `secure` on `NODE_ENV`. Both now gate on a new shared `isRemote()` helper (`@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/env`, the `BUNDLE_ID` signal) — `true` on deployed Managed Runtime (HTTPS), `false` on local `pnpm dev` and `pnpm preview`.

  Previously, on `http://localhost` Safari/WebKit silently refused to persist `Secure` cookies (Chrome and Firefox mask this with a localhost exception), so no auth cookie ever stuck — sign-in and registration redirected straight back to a guest session. `NODE_ENV` was the wrong signal because `pnpm preview` runs a production build over plain HTTP; `BUNDLE_ID` is the same signal that already gates HSTS and `upgrade-insecure-requests`, so cookies, HSTS, and CSP now agree on "is this real HTTPS?". `SameSite=None` cookies (Page Designer design mode) stay `Secure` regardless, as the spec requires. `isRemote()` is also now exported from the SDK and the security-headers middleware consumes it instead of its own private copy.

- #2000 `d8f9066` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Type-narrow `getConfig()`'s client-shaped overloads so client callers see a TypeScript error on `.serverExtension`. Mirrors the existing `useConfig()` narrow — the server overload `getConfig(context)` is unchanged. Reuses the SDK's `ClientFacingAppConfigShape` augmentation slot; un-augmented customers see no behavior change on upgrade.

  Wrappers that take `context?` and forward it continue to compile via the maybe-context overload (also narrowed). Server helpers that need the full shape from a maybe-context call should narrow first (`if (ctx) getConfig(ctx)`) or pass `getConfig<AppConfig>(ctx)`.

- #2458 `5fe6cb1` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Address passkey PR review feedback. Consolidate the duplicate SDK passkey registration surface: widen `auth.webAuthn.authorizeRegistration`/`startRegistration`/`finishRegistration` to work with either a public or private SLAS client (the client secret is now optional, and the `Authorization` Basic-auth header is only sent when a secret is configured), and remove the redundant unreleased `auth.passkey` namespace in favor of `auth.webAuthn`. Gate the seven passkey server routes on `features.passkey.enabled` so they return `404` when the feature is disabled. Add a `parseRequestOptionsFromJSON` capability gate to the passkey login hook and drop the unsafe raw cast so unsupported browsers no longer attempt the ceremony. Surface post-gesture finish failures through a new `onError` channel on `usePasskeyLogin`, wired on both the login page and the checkout contact-info step. Add the missing `account.passkeys` locale keys (`loadError`, `nameTooLong`, `unsupportedBrowser`) and split the flat `uses` key into `uses_one`/`uses_other` plural forms. Per the team convention, all `account.passkeys` strings this feature introduced now reuse the English copy across the non-English locale files, letting them fall back to English until an official translation pass is done rather than shipping self-authored translations. Extract the base64url encoder into a shared `bufferToBase64Url` in `lib/auth/webauthn` so the login assertion path and the registration attestation fallback (browsers lacking `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON`) encode byte-for-byte identically. Bail silently in the login hook when no configured RP ID matches the current hostname, since passing the raw comma-separated list to the WebAuthn API would throw pre-gesture. Add a `405` method guard to the finish-authentication route. Handle the `412` SLAS response on start-authentication as a benign ~1-minute re-attempt throttle by returning silently (mirroring PWA Kit), rather than surfacing it as a `429` "Too many attempts" error. Fix the checkout `LoginModal` password/passwordless login when passkeys are enabled: the modal detects success by watching its fetcher return to idle, but the login action's `redirectDocument` (used to dismiss a lingering passkey picker) unmounts the modal before `onSuccess` fires, so the checkout step never advances and the page hard-reloads. The modal now submits `skipDocumentRedirect` to force the client-side `redirect`, matching the account re-auth path.

- #2096 `89c07df` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Upgrade react-router and @react-router/\* to 7.18.0. Patches an unauthenticated RCE plus four other advisories in the vendored turbo-stream dependency.

  **ACTION REQUIRED (security):** This advisory is only patched once your project resolves `react-router` / `@react-router/*` at `>= 7.18.0`. The SDK declares react-router as a peer dependency, so the version is pinned by your own `package.json`, not by the SDK — bumping `@salesforce/storefront-next-*` alone does not pull the fix. Bump react-router and `@react-router/*` to `7.18.0` in your project's `package.json`. Projects generated fresh from the template already get `7.18.0`.

  This release also renames React Router APIs that stabilized in 7.15 (dropping their `unstable_` prefix). `unstable_optimizeDeps` stays unstable and is unchanged.

  **ACTION REQUIRED — if you ejected `entry.server.tsx` and export your own instrumentations:** React Router 7.18 reads the server-entry export named `instrumentations`, not `unstable_instrumentations`. The framework matches this export by name, so the old name still compiles — it just silently stops registering your instrumentation. Rename `export const unstable_instrumentations` to `export const instrumentations`.

  The remaining renames surface as `pnpm typecheck` errors, so they're caught at build time: `unstable_ServerInstrumentation` → `ServerInstrumentation` (type), route arg `unstable_pattern` → `pattern`, `future.unstable_subResourceIntegrity` → top-level `subResourceIntegrity`, `future.unstable_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests` → `future.v8_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests`, `future.unstable_passThroughRequests` → `future.v8_passThroughRequests`.

  Loader/action/middleware arg _types_ now include a `url: URL` field (RR 7.18 type change). Runtime behavior is unchanged — the framework still provides URLs via `request.url`; only types and test fixtures needed updating. No production loader/action change is required.

- #1977 `ea714d4` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Type-narrow `useConfig()` so server-only namespaces are unreachable from client modules. The SDK now exposes a second augmentation slot, `ClientFacingAppConfigShape`, parallel to `AppConfigShape`; templates fill it with the shape they want `useConfig()` to return (typically `Omit<AppConfig, 'serverExtension'>`). The retail template wires it from its existing `ClientAppConfig` (= `Omit<AppConfig, ServerOnlyNamespace>`), so the runtime extractor (`extractClientConfig`) and the new type narrow read from the same source — adding a server-only namespace to `SERVER_ONLY_NAMESPACES` updates both. `useConfig().serverExtension` is now a TypeScript error in addition to the existing runtime stripping and Vite-build guards. `getConfig()` is unchanged: server callers correctly read `.serverExtension`. Customers who don't fill `ClientFacingAppConfigShape` see no behavior change on upgrade — `useConfig()` falls back to the full `AppConfigShape`.

- #2172 `e88f7f2` Thanks @d-phan_sfemu! - Surface estimated delivery dates on checkout and order confirmation. When the `sfcc.app.shipping.quote` or `sfcc.app.shipping.calculate` ECOM hooks return a `deliveryWindow` (`startAt`/`endAt` RFC 3339 timestamps) on a shipping method or shipment, the storefront now displays the formatted date range. Falls back to existing behavior when `deliveryWindow` is absent.

### Patch Changes

- #2254 `cb90312` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - Bump `happy-dom` from `20.0.10` to `20.8.9` in `packages/storefront-next-runtime` to clear two HIGH-severity advisories (GHSA-w4gp-fjgq-3q4g / CVE-2026-34226 fetch-credentials cookie leak, first patched in `20.8.9`; and GHSA-6q6h-j7hj-3r64 / CVE-2026-33943 ECMAScriptModuleCompiler code injection, first patched in `20.8.8`). `happy-dom` is a devDependency used only as the vitest test environment — never bundled or shipped. The same lockfile refresh floats the transitive `@redocly/openapi-core` forward off the unprovenance `1.34.6` to the provenance-signed `1.34.17`; no `trustPolicyExclude` change is required.

  Note on the sub-dependency churn this pulls in: `1.34.17` exact-pins older `@redocly/ajv` (`8.17.2` → `8.11.2`) and `@redocly/config` (`0.22.2` → `0.22.0`), and `@redocly/ajv@8.11.2` swaps `fast-uri` for a new transitive `uri-js-replace@1.0.1`. The two apparent backward moves are fresh resolutions on a package that moved _forward_ (not provenance regressions of an already-trusted pin), so the `no-downgrade` install gate does not trip. All of this is dev-only openapi-typescript codegen tooling — never bundled or shipped.

- #2264 `628aac2` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - Update SCAPI client from the latest OpenAPI specs published to Anypoint Exchange (ECOM v26.7 API surface, generated 2026-07-08). Notably adds `PageMetaTag.type` on shopper-products (`name` / `property` / `title` / `jsonld`).

  Specs are pulled as "latest matching major", so several land ahead of the versions commerce-sdk-isomorphic `main` pins for the same nominal ECOM release; the diffs are additive.

- #2543 `21fdcfb` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Support WebAuthn (passkey) authentication (login) on public SLAS clients. `auth.webAuthn.startAuthentication` and `finishAuthentication` no longer throw `Client secret is required for WebAuthn operations` when no `clientSecret` is configured — the SLAS WebAuthn authentication endpoints accept an optional HTTP Basic `Authorization` header, so the header is now sent only for private clients and omitted for public clients (which authenticate via `client_id` in the request body). This matches the public/private handling already used by the `webAuthn.*Registration` methods.

  `auth.webAuthn.authorizeRegistration` now rejects `mode: 'sms'` with a clear error before calling SLAS. SLAS does not support SMS delivery for WebAuthn passkey authorization — the endpoint rejects it with a 400 (`PWDLESS_INVALID_MODE`) — so only `'email'` and `'callback'` are valid.

- #2327 `6616f5b` Thanks @s-hussain_sfemu! - Enable the full `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` recommended rule set (plus `no-aria-hidden-on-focusable` and `anchor-ambiguous-text`) so accessibility defects are caught at lint time. A few intentional patterns (autofocus on section open, arrow-key navigation within swatch and option groups, the labelled carousel region, and Page Designer edit-mode drag handles) keep scoped inline disables and change no runtime behavior.

  Pins `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y>minimatch` to `3.1.2` via `pnpm.overrides`. The plugin's rule resolution (notably `label-has-associated-control`) depends on minimatch v3 glob semantics; a transitive bump to v10 changes brace/negation handling and silently breaks that rule. Keep this pin until the plugin declares v10 support — do not remove it in a routine dependency bump.

- #2368 `45d425f` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Make the `currency` cookie JS-readable (`httpOnly:false`) so the storefront can restore the selected currency on the client under a cached app shell. Scoped to the currency cookie only — the site and locale cookies remain `httpOnly:true`.

- #2273 `1dbb367` Thanks @emmyzhang_sfemu! - Fix external Page Designer content links that were entered without a URL scheme. `buildUrl` now recognizes explicit schemes (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `https:`, etc.) and normalizes scheme-less bare domains (e.g. `www.google.com`) to `https://`, so they navigate to the external site instead of being mangled into a site-prefixed internal path like `/global/en-GBwww.google.com`.

- #2482 `8dde3e3` Thanks @michael-mcmahon_sfemu! - Remove live `oxlint-disable` exceptions that were fixable outright: rewrite the `no-unsafe-optional-chaining` test assertions to hoist the type-asserted optional chain into a local before dereferencing, and convert the `consistent-type-imports` imports (`NormalizedApiError`, `buttonVariants`) to `import type` / inline `type`. Document why `typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` stays off (tsgolint false-positive storm) in README-LINTING.md. No runtime behavior changes.

- #2482 `8dde3e3` Thanks @michael-mcmahon_sfemu! - Rename inline `eslint-disable*` suppression directives to `oxlint-disable*` and remove a dead `// prettier-ignore`. The lint toolchain migrated to OxLint + Biome, but the carried-over comments still named the removed tools; OxLint honors both prefixes identically, so this is an enforcement-neutral clarity change (comments now name the actual linter). No rules, severities, or suppressed findings changed.

- #2329 `b97e72b` Thanks @emmyzhang_sfemu! - Remove the move and delete handles from the root component on the Page Designer design-mode canvas. When editing a single content block in the focused visual canvas (the `preview/component` route), the block can no longer be moved or deleted from its canvas toolbar — it stays selectable and configurable, and its nested children keep their own handles. Implemented via a new opt-in `RootComponentProvider` (from `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/design/react/core`) that the preview route wraps around the previewed component; the design decorators read it to suppress the root's move/delete affordances. No effect at runtime or when the provider is absent.

- #2488 `e473a58` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - Update SCAPI client from the latest OpenAPI specs published to Anypoint Exchange (shopper-search-v1 1.10.0 → 1.12.0; 1.11.0 skipped, no intermediate changes dropped). Changes are strictly additive at the type level — new optional `slug` field on `ProductSearchHit`, new optional `personalized` query param, and `slug` added to the product-search `expand` union — so runtime SDK behavior is unchanged.

- #2393 `d706339` Thanks @emmyzhang_sfemu! - Fix mini-PD content block editor: components rendered permanently selected/unclickable. Fall back to the component `id` when a block has no `contentLinkUuid` so selection/hover identity is never the empty string (which collided with the empty-string selection default).

  Also fix the design frame's name label being clipped when a component sits flush to the top of the canvas (as in the content block editor): the label now renders inside the top edge instead of above it when there isn't room.

- #2555 `2606a3f` Thanks @d-phan_sfemu! - Allow Google Maps origins in the default CSP so checkout address autocomplete works: add `https://places.googleapis.com` and `https://maps.googleapis.com` to `connect-src` (Places autocomplete requests) and add `https://maps.googleapis.com` to `script-src` (the Maps JS loader script).

Now that the template emits prefixed paths (`/uk/cart`, `/global/en-GB/cart`), that stacked the locale a second time and SFRA 404'd. The proxy now reads `app.url.prefix` and the site/locale alias catalog from `config.server.ts`, strips the prefix the URL already carries, and reuses that site/locale when decorating to SFRA's `/s/{siteId}/{locale}/…` shape — for no prefix, `/:localeId`, and `/:siteId/:localeId` alike. A captured segment is only treated as a site/locale when it is a known identifier, so a bare legacy path (`/cart` under `/:localeId`) isn't mistaken for a locale home. The root `/` maps to the locale-less SFRA site root and the query string is preserved across the rewrite.

  `hybridProxyPlugin` gains optional `urlPrefix`, `siteAliases`, `localeAliases`, and a last-resort `rewritePath` escape hatch for non-standard URL models. `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` exports a new `extractPrefixParamValues` site-context helper (mirrors `stripPathPrefix`'s matching rules) that powers the prefix-aware rewrite.

- #2222 `c016b62` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Add lazy data-store preference middleware and an opt-in cross-request L1 cache to cut DynamoDB reads on the single shared data-store partition

  The eager `dataStoreMiddleware` reads all four preference entries on every request that reaches root, even routes that never use them. All entries share one partition key (`"${MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID} ${DEPLOY_TARGET}"`), so that volume can throttle one physical partition under load.

  The new lazy variants (`customSitePreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `customGlobalPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `gcpPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `loginPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, their `get*Lazy` accessors, and the `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy` bundle) register a memoized loader instead of fetching up front, so the read fires only when a loader reads the value and repeat reads within a request share the promise. The eager exports are deprecated but unchanged. The template wires `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy`, reads login preferences via the async `getLoginPreferences` wrapper, and moves the GCP Address Autocomplete API key onto the checkout loader (the only route mounting `GoogleCloudApiProvider`).

  The L1 cache serves repeat reads of the same entry from memory. It lives on `globalThis` (via a `Symbol.for` key) to survive SSR module re-evaluation and persist across a warm Lambda's sequential requests. Only successful reads of deployment-/site-scoped preference entries are cached — never shopper data, fallbacks, missing entries, or errors; `getDataStoreEntry` stays a thin, cache-free read. It is off by default; set `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_ENABLED=true` to opt in per environment (e.g. deployed MRT). `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_TTL` sets the TTL in ms (default 300000) and `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_MAXBYTES` the total-value byte budget (default 131072); zero/negative/non-numeric falls back to the default. The cache is bounded by byte size, not entry count, evicting least-recently-used keys. `clearDataStoreCache()` drops the instance for test isolation or to force-bust a warm container after a preference publish.

- #1994 `8874f57` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Add an internal CSP "contributor" mechanism (`CspContributor` interface, `resolveCsp`, boot-time guardrails + observability, bounded per-request body cache). No change to shipped security headers — this is the foundation for feature-aware CSP (shopper agent, Page Designer) landing next.

- #2042 `c0b87fb` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Shopper agent (Embedded Messaging) now contributes its exact configured origins to the CSP instead of relying on broad wildcards. The security middleware accepts boot-static CSP contributors; the template ships a shopper-agent contributor that derives script/frame/connect origins from `commerceAgent` config. The SDK now exports `normalizeCspOrigin` / `inspectCspOrigin` — the single source of truth for CSP-origin safety rules, shared by the boot-time contributor validator and the template normalizer so they cannot drift. Adds the `add-csp-contributor` skill for authoring new contributors. No change to shipped headers when shopper agent is disabled.

- #2023 `37d9aee` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Stop marking cookies `Secure` in local development so Safari can persist them. The template's `getCookieConfig` (auth, basket, shopper-context, turnstile cookies) hardcoded `secure: true`, and the SDK's site-context cookies (`site_id`, `lng`, `currency`) gated `secure` on `NODE_ENV`. Both now gate on a new shared `isRemote()` helper (`@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/env`, the `BUNDLE_ID` signal) — `true` on deployed Managed Runtime (HTTPS), `false` on local `pnpm dev` and `pnpm preview`.

  Previously, on `http://localhost` Safari/WebKit silently refused to persist `Secure` cookies (Chrome and Firefox mask this with a localhost exception), so no auth cookie ever stuck — sign-in and registration redirected straight back to a guest session. `NODE_ENV` was the wrong signal because `pnpm preview` runs a production build over plain HTTP; `BUNDLE_ID` is the same signal that already gates HSTS and `upgrade-insecure-requests`, so cookies, HSTS, and CSP now agree on "is this real HTTPS?". `SameSite=None` cookies (Page Designer design mode) stay `Secure` regardless, as the spec requires. `isRemote()` is also now exported from the SDK and the security-headers middleware consumes it instead of its own private copy.

- #2000 `d8f9066` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Type-narrow `getConfig()`'s client-shaped overloads so client callers see a TypeScript error on `.serverExtension`. Mirrors the existing `useConfig()` narrow — the server overload `getConfig(context)` is unchanged. Reuses the SDK's `ClientFacingAppConfigShape` augmentation slot; un-augmented customers see no behavior change on upgrade.

  Wrappers that take `context?` and forward it continue to compile via the maybe-context overload (also narrowed). Server helpers that need the full shape from a maybe-context call should narrow first (`if (ctx) getConfig(ctx)`) or pass `getConfig<AppConfig>(ctx)`.

- #2096 `89c07df` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Upgrade react-router and @react-router/\* to 7.18.0. Patches an unauthenticated RCE plus four other advisories in the vendored turbo-stream dependency.

  **ACTION REQUIRED (security):** This advisory is only patched once your project resolves `react-router` / `@react-router/*` at `>= 7.18.0`. The SDK declares react-router as a peer dependency, so the version is pinned by your own `package.json`, not by the SDK — bumping `@salesforce/storefront-next-*` alone does not pull the fix. Bump react-router and `@react-router/*` to `7.18.0` in your project's `package.json`. Projects generated fresh from the template already get `7.18.0`.

  This release also renames React Router APIs that stabilized in 7.15 (dropping their `unstable_` prefix). `unstable_optimizeDeps` stays unstable and is unchanged.

  **ACTION REQUIRED — if you ejected `entry.server.tsx` and export your own instrumentations:** React Router 7.18 reads the server-entry export named `instrumentations`, not `unstable_instrumentations`. The framework matches this export by name, so the old name still compiles — it just silently stops registering your instrumentation. Rename `export const unstable_instrumentations` to `export const instrumentations`.

  The remaining renames surface as `pnpm typecheck` errors, so they're caught at build time: `unstable_ServerInstrumentation` → `ServerInstrumentation` (type), route arg `unstable_pattern` → `pattern`, `future.unstable_subResourceIntegrity` → top-level `subResourceIntegrity`, `future.unstable_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests` → `future.v8_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests`, `future.unstable_passThroughRequests` → `future.v8_passThroughRequests`.

  Loader/action/middleware arg _types_ now include a `url: URL` field (RR 7.18 type change). Runtime behavior is unchanged — the framework still provides URLs via `request.url`; only types and test fixtures needed updating. No production loader/action change is required.

- #1900 `39b9c15` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Add default security response headers middleware (`createSecurityHeadersMiddleware` exported from `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/security`). Ships strict defaults for CSP (with per-request nonce), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy. Customers extend defaults via `config.server.ts`; `defaultCspDirectives` is exported for spread.

- #1977 `ea714d4` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Type-narrow `useConfig()` so server-only namespaces are unreachable from client modules. The SDK now exposes a second augmentation slot, `ClientFacingAppConfigShape`, parallel to `AppConfigShape`; templates fill it with the shape they want `useConfig()` to return (typically `Omit<AppConfig, 'serverExtension'>`). The retail template wires it from its existing `ClientAppConfig` (= `Omit<AppConfig, ServerOnlyNamespace>`), so the runtime extractor (`extractClientConfig`) and the new type narrow read from the same source — adding a server-only namespace to `SERVER_ONLY_NAMESPACES` updates both. `useConfig().serverExtension` is now a TypeScript error in addition to the existing runtime stripping and Vite-build guards. `getConfig()` is unchanged: server callers correctly read `.serverExtension`. Customers who don't fill `ClientFacingAppConfigShape` see no behavior change on upgrade — `useConfig()` falls back to the full `AppConfigShape`.

- #1912 `43ba4ba` Thanks @j-ha_sfemu! - Add WebAuthn API support to the SCAPI auth helper (`scapi-client/auth`). Includes typed functions and types for passkey registration, authentication, and credential management.

### Patch Changes

- #2166 `03b4ccd` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - Automate SCAPI client spec updates. A new `scapi:update-specs` script downloads the latest released OpenAPI specs from Anypoint Exchange, swaps the spec folders, rewrites `redocly.yaml`, and regenerates the client; a weekly `SCAPI Spec Update` CI workflow runs it, opens a PR, and posts it to Slack so the shipped client never drifts behind the live APIs. Also repairs a malformed `shopper-experience` spec version (`1.50` → `1.5.0`) that was silently masking drift, and flags any non-semver tracked version loudly instead of mis-comparing it.

- #2028 `ec0a077` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - Re-enable manifest-driven page resolution for pages that declare data bindings. The temporary patch that returned `null` (forcing a SCAPI fallback) when a page manifest declared data bindings has been removed, so these pages now resolve from the manifest like any other. Tracked under.

- #2249 `fb644b6` Thanks @a-mcguire_sfemu! - Render embedded content block children as static, non-interactive content in Page Designer design mode automatically. Embedded blocks and their children are fetched separately by the storefront (via `getComponent`) rather than by the host (via `getPage`), so the host cannot resolve them for select / delete / move.

  Detection is declarative: the embedded owner declares its subtree to the SDK via `EmbeddedSubtreeProvider` (wired into the template's `EmbeddedComponentRegion` from the owner's own `embedded` flag), and the design decorators read it via `useIsWithinEmbeddedSubtree`. The owner's `embedded` flag is the sole source of truth — there is no page-membership inference — so an empty embedded region is covered just like a populated one.

- #2016 `f7786e4` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Suppress the CSP `upgrade-insecure-requests` directive in local development. The security headers middleware now drops it when running locally (`BUNDLE_ID` unset or `'local'`), mirroring the existing HSTS gate; deployed (Managed Runtime) responses are unchanged and still send the directive.

  Previously it was emitted on `pnpm dev`, which serves plain HTTP over loopback. Safari/WebKit honors the directive literally and upgrades `http://localhost` subresources to `https://` on the same (non-TLS) port, so every CSS/JS request failed with a TLS error and the page rendered unstyled. Chrome and Firefox masked the bug by skipping the upgrade for loopback addresses.

### Patch Changes

- #1988 `871cf56` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Remove pilot/beta service disclaimers and pilot-only documentation links from package READMEs now that Storefront Next is generally available at v1.0.0. The retail template README now points to the published developer docs at developer.salesforce.com instead of the gated pilot docs site.

## 1.0.0

### Minor Changes

- #1823 `0a3fcdc` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - w:

  Tighten the `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/config` public surface for V1 GA.

  **Removed from public exports** (followups to #1741):
  - `ConfigContext` — internal React context backing `useConfig()`. Read config via `useConfig()` instead.
  - `createAppConfig` — one-line `.app` accessor with no semantic value. Use `staticConfig.app` directly.
  - The `middleware.ts` source file and `createAppConfigMiddleware` factory were also deleted; they had B2C-Commerce-specific validation hardcoded in (`commerce.api.{clientId,organizationId,shortCode}`, `SCAPI_PROXY_HOST`) and the retail template ships its own validating middleware. Future templates write their own.

  **Added** — `AppConfigShape` interface as a module-augmentation hook for `getConfig()` / `useConfig()` typing. Each template `declare module`s once in its own types file and gets typed access without the per-call `<AppConfig>` generic:

  ```ts
  // In your template's src/types/config.ts:
  declare module "@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/config" {
    interface AppConfigShape extends AppConfig {}
  }
  ```

  **Other changes**
  - `Locale`, `Site`, `Url` JSDoc reframed as opt-in baseline shapes — `BaseConfig<App>` is generic so future templates can ignore them.
  - `defineConfig` JSDoc now explicitly notes it reads `process.env` at call time (server-only side effect).
  - `mergeEnvConfig`'s engagement-specific protected-paths error message is now generic.
  - Retail-flavored examples in `schema.ts` / `utils.ts` JSDoc neutralized.
  - Template (`template-retail-rsc-app`): all 110+ `getConfig<AppConfig>()` / `useConfig<AppConfig>()` call sites now use the augmented hook (no per-call generic).
  - Template `commerce.sites: Site[]` now imports the richer `Site` shape from `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/site-context` (reconciles the duplicate `Site` types that existed across both subpaths).
  - `contact-info.tsx` migrated from `useContext(ConfigContext)` to `useConfig()` (the only production caller of the bypass pattern).
  - README-CONFIG.md fixed: `loadConfig` subpath was wrong (`/load-config` → `/config/load-config`); `appConfigContext` now documented for custom middleware composition; `AppConfigShape` augmentation pattern documented.

  Public surface delta: 13 runtime + 5 type exports → 5 + 6 (plus `loadConfig` at the separate `./config/load-config` subpath).

  > **Semver note for future maintainers:** This entry is a `minor` bump _only because the package is still pre-V1 GA_. Removing public exports is a `major` once V1 ships — do not paste this pattern after lock-in.

- #1787 `d39ccce` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Remove internal data-store context objects and key constants from public exports (`sitePreferencesContext`, `customGlobalPreferencesContext`, `gcpPreferencesContext`, `loginPreferencesContext`, `DEFAULT_SITE_PREFERENCES_KEY`, `DEFAULT_CUSTOM_GLOBAL_PREFERENCES_KEY`, `DEFAULT_GCP_PREFERENCES_KEY`) and remove subpath entry points (`./data-store/custom-site-preferences`, `./data-store/custom-global-preferences`, `./data-store/gcp-preferences`) — these are internal plumbing that allows bypassing middleware invariants.

- #1744 `2f00128` Thanks @clavery_sfemu! - Add `BUILT_IN_CLIENT_DEFAULTS` (and `BUILT_IN_CLIENT_KEYS`, `isBuiltInClientKey`) — a single source of truth for per-built-in-client config (basePath, locale-awareness) consumed by both `createCommerceApiClients` and the dev CLI's SCAPI override codegen. `createCommerceApiClients` now drives its baseUrl + globalParams selection from this map so the two never drift

- #1655 `a69fb13` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - Add `createLazyDataStoreMiddleware` and `readLazyDataStoreEntry` exports under `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/data-store`. The lazy variant stores a memoized loader in router context instead of fetching up front, so routes that never read the entry never pay for the data-store call. Repeated reads within the same request share the in-flight promise. Internal `loadDataStoreEntry` helper unifies the eager and lazy fetch + error paths.

- #1655 `a69fb13` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - Add MRT-side attribute resolution for Page Designer manifests : `processPage` now walks each component's `data` map through a type-driven dispatch table that converts manifest envelopes into the same wire shape SCAPI's `getPage` controller would have returned. Covers `image` (URL resolution via `resolveMediaUrl`), `file` (envelope → URL string), `markup` (`?$staticlink$` placeholder rewriting via the new `rewriteMarkup` helper), and `cms_record` (recursive dispatch of inner attributes). Unknown attribute types pass through unchanged with a deduped one-time warning for forward compatibility. Pipeline-action placeholders (`$link-...$`, `$url(...)$`, `$include(...)$`) are intentionally not rewritten — storefront-next uses React composition for navigation. Module is platform-neutral; callers inject an `AttributeResolutionContext` (host, `resolveMediaUrl`, optional `pageLibraryDomain`).

- #1671 `d65150a` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Add Shopper Availability v1.1.0 SCAPI client (`clients.shopperAvailability`) for retrieving product inventory availability without loading full product details

- #1460 `95147eb` Thanks @j-ha_sfemu! - Email Verification Feature - Account Details

- #1655 `a69fb13` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - Extend `PageManifest` with optional `componentTypes` (per-`typeId` attribute definitions hoisted by the manifest builder) and `pageLibraryDomain` (used by the markup URL rewriter). Both are optional so older manifests still load. `componentInfo` entries gain optional `name`, `fragment`, and `custom` fields, and previously-required `visibilityRules`/`regions` are now optional (omitted when empty). `RegionInfo` fields (`name`, `componentTypeExclusions`, `componentTypeInclusions`, `maxComponents`) shift from `T | null` to optional-and-omitted to match the on-the-wire compact shape.

- #1475 `34dea88` Thanks @j-ha_sfemu! - Update shopper-customers OAS from v1.3.2 to v1.8.0 and replace shopper-login OAS v1.42.2 with auth OAS v1.47.0

- #1623 `38d828f` Thanks @j-ha_sfemu! - Update Shopper Login/Auth OAS to 1.48.0 and Shopper Customers OAS to 1.8.0

- #1907 `3c9c3e5` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Add default security response headers middleware (`createSecurityHeadersMiddleware` exported from `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/security`). Ships strict defaults for CSP (with per-request nonce), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy. Customers extend defaults via `config.server.ts`; `defaultCspDirectives` is exported for spread.

### Patch Changes

- #1927 `b370405` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Demote expected DataStoreNotFoundError logs from warn to debug to eliminate dev server log noise

- #1934 `f7e9554` Thanks @mjuraschik_sfemu! - Security middleware: relax `frame-ancestors` only on Page Designer / Business Manager preview requests (`?mode=EDIT|PREVIEW`). On those requests the SDK extends `frame-ancestors` to allow Salesforce-owned admin host families (`*.unified.demandware.net`, `*.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, `*.demandware.net`) and suppresses `X-Frame-Options` (which has no host-list form). Normal shopper traffic continues to ship `frame-ancestors 'self'` and `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`. Customers who already extend `frame-ancestors` themselves are unaffected — their override is respected verbatim across all requests.

- #1888 `d355c50` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - Fall back to SCAPI page resolution when the page manifest declares data bindings. The manifest-driven resolver cannot resolve bindings yet (planned for 26.7), so it now returns `null` and lets the caller fetch the page from SCAPI instead. Tracked under.

- #1779 `8ae7030` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Stop the data-store middleware from crashing MRT requests on transient DAL failures. `DataStoreServiceError` and `DataStoreUnavailableError` now both honor `onUnavailable`, and the four built-in middlewares (`customSitePreferencesMiddleware`, `customGlobalPreferencesMiddleware`, `gcpPreferencesMiddleware`, `loginPreferencesMiddleware`) default to `'fallback'` so the request continues with the configured fallback value instead of throwing. `SFNEXT_DATA_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_MODE` is preserved as an opt-in escape hatch — set it to `'throw'` to restore fail-fast behavior. `DataStoreNotFoundError` keeps its existing missing-state semantics; errors thrown from `transform` still propagate. `createDataStoreMiddleware`'s factory default for customer-authored middlewares stays at `'throw'` (no change to the public API contract).

  Adds `dataStoreLoggerContext`, `getDataStoreLogger`, and the `DataStoreLogger` interface under `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/data-store`. Hosts can inject a request-scoped structured logger so SDK warnings emit with `correlationId`, `method`, and `path` bindings instead of bare `console.warn`. The storefront template's `loggingMiddleware` wires this automatically; when unset, falls back to a console-based logger that fail-soft serializes metadata (cyclic / unserializable values won't crash the request).

- #1948 `3535909` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Allow the OOTB Einstein engagement adapter through the default CSP. The adapter fires browser `navigator.sendBeacon` calls to the CQuotient activities API (`https://api.cquotient.com/v3/activities/...`), which is governed by `connect-src`. The default `connect-src` did not list that host, so every Einstein beacon (viewPage, viewProduct, viewCategory, …) was blocked by CSP and reported a console violation on a freshly generated project. Added `https://api.cquotient.com` to the default `connect-src` directive.

- #1939 `d273772` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - Fix three dev-server console errors in freshly generated projects (`pnpm dev`):
  - **Invalid hook call / "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')"**: on first dev load Vite discovered the React-importing runtime SDK entry points (`/config`, `/security/react`, `/site-context`, `/design/react/core`, `/routing/app-wrapper`, `/i18n/client`) lazily at request time, triggering a dep re-optimization + full reload that transiently loaded a second React instance. Also pre-bundles the i18n peer deps the SDK imports internally but the template does not import from its own source (`i18next-browser-languagedetector`, used by `/i18n/client`; and `remix-i18next/middleware`, used by the SDK's `/i18n` barrel) — these are discovered late for the same reason. (`react-i18next` needs no entry: the template imports it directly, so Vite's initial source crawl already finds it.) All are now in the first-pass `optimizeDeps.include`, so a single optimization runs with one shared React and no mid-session reload.
  - **CSP blocked the Vite HMR websocket** (`ws://localhost:24678`): the security middleware now appends `ws://localhost:*`, `ws://127.0.0.1:*`, and `wss://localhost:*` to `connect-src` only when running locally (`BUNDLE_ID` unset or `local`). Deployed/MRT responses are unchanged.
  - **Nonce hydration mismatch** on the inline `window.__APP_CONFIG__` script: browsers strip the `nonce` content attribute from the DOM after applying CSP, so the client saw `nonce=""` against the server's real value. Added `suppressHydrationWarning` to that script element; the CSP nonce still applies.

- #1898 `dee3c0a` Thanks @mjuraschik_sfemu! - Fall back to category-level page assignment during manifest resolution when a product-keyed page lookup misses. `resolveDynamicPageId` and `resolvePage` now accept an optional `categoryId` (string or Promise) consulted only after the product lookup misses, and the Page Designer resolution middleware threads the request's categoryId through whenever a productId is also present.

- #1409 `55f8c1b` Thanks @j-ha_sfemu! - Exclude OTP endpoints from auth token invalidation — 401 responses from `/oauth2/otp/` now surface as normal API errors instead of triggering `AuthTokenInvalidError`

- #1708 `bdd4365` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Make `@react-router/dev` and `@react-router/fs-routes` optional peer dependencies to avoid dependency conflicts for consumers that only use the `/design` exports

- #1655 `a69fb13` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - `processPage` now requires `defaultLocale` and `attrCtx` in its `PageProcessorContext` and accepts an optional `componentTypes` map. Component `data` is composed in priority order (active-locale content → default-locale content → `attrDef.defaultValue`) when type definitions are available, falling back to the legacy spread merge when they aren't. Top-level page `data` is also resolved when present.

- #1744 `2f00128` Thanks @clavery_sfemu! - Re-export `createAuthHelpers` from the SCAPI entry point so the template can rebuild `clients.auth` against an overridden `shopperLogin` client

- #1741 `9152bc4` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Remove internal config utilities from public exports (`pathToObject`, `parseEnvValue`, `extractValidPaths`, `mergeEnvConfig`, `MergeEnvConfigOptions`, `createAppConfigMiddleware`, `deepMerge`) — these are internal plumbing and should not be part of the V1 GA public surface

- #1703 `f405241` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Remove `usid` from `PasswordlessExchangeTokenOptions` and the `exchangeToken` implementation — `usid` is not a valid field in the SLAS `PasswordLessLoginTokenRequest` schema (auth-oas-1.48.0) and was silently ignored by the server

- #1699 `5ee459a` Thanks @alex-vuong_sfemu! - Unify sanitizePrefix and stripPathPrefix into one helper

- #1655 `a69fb13` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - `VariationEntry.page` now carries SCAPI-shape page metadata (`name`, `aspectTypeId`, `description`, `pageTitle`, `pageDescription`, `pageKeywords`) populated by the manifest builder; non-default-locale overrides live on a new `pageContent` overlay applied at request time.

- #1834 `0d500de` Thanks @ssojka_sfemu! - Coerce string values returned by the data binding API into typed values when resolving expressions. The data provider returns every field as a string, so `"true"`/`"false"` are now resolved to booleans and numeric strings (e.g. `"2026"`, `"-12.5"`) to numbers. Strings that aren't booleans or finite numbers — including empty/whitespace-only strings and HTML — pass through unchanged.

## v0.4.0 (May 5, 2026)

- Design layer: Add `contentLinkUuid` support for duplicate component handling
  - Make `contentLinkUuid` required on component interaction events (select, delete, move, hover, focus)
  - Add `fragmentId` support to drag-and-drop events for content block instances
  - Design state fields (`selected`, `hovered`, `focused`) now expose `contentLinkUuid` as the primary identifier instead of `componentId`
  - Regions track `contentLinkUuids` instead of `componentIds`, enabling correct self-drop detection and drag validation for duplicate components
- Bump `@salesforce/mrt-utilities` to 0.1.6 to fix strict `express@5.1.0` peer dependency (now accepts `^4.0.0 || ^5.0.0`)
- Update Shopper Experience API spec to v1.3.0 with `contentLinkUuid` field support
  - Add `contentLinkUuid` to Component schema for content link UUID tracking
  - Add `name`, `fragment`, `localized`, `visible` fields to Component schema
  - Regenerate TypeScript types for all SCAPI clients
  - Remove unused `@ts-expect-error` directives from page processor now that schema includes the missing fields
- Unify data-store access on `DataStore.getDataStore().getEntry()` from `@salesforce/mrt-utilities/data-store`; remove legacy provider abstraction/local fallback paths and related tests (#1533)
- Re-export `DataStore` and data-store error types from `@salesforce/mrt-utilities/data-store` to align runtime APIs with upstream package structure (#1533)
- Add `/i18n` and `/i18n/client` subpath exports: `createI18nMiddleware`, `getTranslation`, `getLocale`, `mockI18nContext`, `initI18next`, and shared `defaultInterpolation`
- Unify data-store access on `DataStore.getDataStore().getEntry()` from `@salesforce/mrt-utilities/data-store`; remove legacy provider abstraction/local fallback paths and related tests (#1533)
- Re-export `DataStore` and data-store error types from `@salesforce/mrt-utilities/data-store` to align runtime APIs with upstream package structure (#1533)
- Add login preferences middleware and context to data store (#1453)
- Extend `SiteProvider` to accept `site`, `language`, `locale`, `currency` props and `useSite()` to return `SiteContextValue` (#1384)
- Add support to MRT Data Layer access #1215
- Add currency detection to site-context middleware (#1342)
- Add runtime support for custom API client typing and proxy client composition
- Add support for OOTB API Key for Google Address Autocomplete feature from MRT Data Layer (#1509)
